answer: One concrete defense: cap the total voting weight the network admits each epoch, then hand out that fixed trickle through a verifiable-random lottery weighted by each identity's proof of distinct behavior. Trust regrows slowly, like timber in a managed forest, so a sybil farm can no longer mint unlimited free identities; its clones compete against each other for one scarce island of slots. Every admission leaves a quill-stroke signature on a public log, so any later attempt to inflate weight is detectable by anyone.
